topics.headline: opening conjunction continues the verdict
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears 19:80 as a coordinated continuation of the judgment sequence in 19:79, not as a fresh independent start.
topics.reason: The aligned word is a conjunctive prefix, and the attachment evidence treats the following inheritance clause as the first verbal clause carried forward from the prior judgment sequence.

words.gloss_range: divine inheriting or reclaiming in which the boaster and the content of his boast are brought under one dispossessing verb
words.root_gloss_range: root range around inheritance, what remains after departure, succession, transfer to an heir, and divine remaining ownership; the local form selects divine inheriting as reversal of human ownership claims
words.prose: {{ar:وَنَرِثُهُ}} ({{tr:wa-narithuhu}}) compresses the coordinated verdict, divine first-person agency, and the boaster as attached object into one word. The verb then stretches over both the man and what he says, so inheritance is not only loss of property but loss of the person and the claim he made; speech itself becomes estate-like residue. The {{ar:و ر ث}} ({{tr:w-r-th}}) field makes the boast of ownership sound temporary: what he presented as possession becomes residue returning to the true inheritor, reversing believer-gift inheritance patterns (7:43, 39:74, 40:53). This also sets the ayah's architecture, moving from inherited person and speech toward compelled solitary arrival, while the inherited-aloneness pairing reverses the plea not to be left alone (21:89). Across the boundary from 19:79, the recorded speaker is no longer only warned about; he is grammatically seized as the object of possession.

topics.headline: divine agency and human object are bound into the verb
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees divine action carried by the prefix while the boaster is reduced to an attached object inside the same word.
topics.reason: The local form is first-person plural with a third-person masculine object suffix, and the suffix is resolved to the prior claimant.

topics.headline: one inheritance frame seizes person and speech
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the verb reaches both the boaster and the content of his speech, making the uttered claim part of what is reclaimed.
topics.reason: The attachment evidence marks both the clitic object and the following relative content object under the inheritance verb, so the double-dispossession reading is locally licensed.

topics.headline: inheritance reverses the ownership boast
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels the legal estate image reverse the claim of wealth and children into something left behind and taken by God.
topics.reason: The local root profile supports divine inheritance, while the inter-ayah contrasts with inheritance granted to others (7:128, 7:43, 39:74, 40:53) and divine ultimate inheriting (19:40) sharpen the reversal without changing the local parse.

topics.headline: inheritance opens the dispossession-to-arrival scene
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the inheritance verb as the first stage in a scene that ends with the claimant arriving alone.
topics.reason: The clauses coordinate inheriting and coming, and the inheritance-alone contrast with Zakariyya's plea (21:89) gives the local arc a concrete intertextual pressure.

topics.headline: boundary shifts from warning record to possession
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the prior warning cross the ayah boundary into a settled act of divine possession.
topics.reason: The same claimant is carried across the boundary as the object of the inheritance verb, moving the discourse from announced recording to possession-closure.

words.gloss_range: relative object marker that turns the boaster's saying into the content-domain inherited by the preceding verb
words.prose: {{ar:مَا}} ({{tr:mā}}) turns the next verb into the inherited content-domain. It makes the boast grammatically subordinate to the inheritance frame, while its scope can still point both to the specific claim already made in 19:77 and to whatever speech belongs to that boastful register.

topics.headline: relative marker makes speech inheritable
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the following saying clause is not independent speech but the object-domain governed by divine inheritance.
topics.reason: The local syntax marks the word as a relative pronoun and direct object, with the following saying verb inside its relative clause.

topics.headline: specific boast and wider claim-scope both remain
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the particle reach the concrete boast of 19:77 while also leaving the wording open enough for the whole class of such claims.
topics.reason: Prior context anchors the content to the boast in 19:77, but the relative form itself can carry a broader whatever-he-says scope inside that local frame.

words.gloss_range: ongoing or habitual saying whose content is subordinated as the inherited speech-claim
words.root_gloss_range: broad speech, saying, report, claim, and verbal stance range; the local imperfect selects ongoing saying whose content becomes accountable property under the inheritance frame
words.prose: {{ar:يَقُولُ}} ({{tr:yaqūlu}}) keeps the claimant present as a third-person verbal subject without renaming him. Because the verb sits under the preceding relative marker, the speech is no longer merely reported; it becomes the content God inherits and the liability left by the boast. The imperfect form keeps the boast active or habitual at the point of seizure, and the {{ar:ق و ل}} ({{tr:q-w-l}}) speech field is pulled from human assertion into divine accounting. The repeated speech phrase from 19:79 now moves from record to possession, then onward toward the coming-alone clause. That reversal also sets 19:80 against presumptuous inheritors who speak in 7:169, against prophetic receiving in 19:30, and against the original wealth-and-children boast in 19:77.

topics.headline: imperfect verb keeps the same speaker active
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the same claimant carried forward by verbal morphology while the imperfect keeps his boast active rather than sealed as a distant quotation.
topics.reason: The local verb is third-person masculine imperfect with a pro-dropped subject, matching the prior claimant without introducing a new named subject.

topics.headline: speech becomes the inherited accountability object
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees speech itself become the residue of liability that God claims, not just a line of dialogue.
topics.reason: The relative object is governed by the inheritance verb, and the exact phrase from 19:79 is now processed through possession rather than only recording.

topics.headline: speech pivots into compelled arrival
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the boast that began the polemic turn into the bridge toward the claimant's compelled arrival.
topics.reason: The local order places the saying clause before the coming clause, while the contrast with the boast of being given (19:77) and the demand for a sign to come (20:133) makes the speech-arrival reversal concrete.

topics.headline: same speech crosses from record to possession
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the same speech material from 19:79 move across the boundary from written evidence into inherited property.
topics.reason: The phrase from 19:79 is repeated in the next ayah under a new governing divine verb, and the same third-person morphology preserves the speaker continuity.

topics.headline: other speech-inheritance scenes sharpen the reversal
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees this local speech claim set against other scenes where saying and reception are morally reversed.
topics.reason: The contrast with scripture-inheritors who speak presumptuously (7:169), prophetic receiving (19:30), and the original boast (19:77) is concrete inter-ayah evidence but does not override the local speech-as-object grammar.

words.gloss_range: internal coordinator that joins divine inheriting to the human's coming as parts of one accountability sequence
words.prose: The second {{ar:و}} ({{tr:wa}}) is the ayah's internal hinge. It keeps the coming-alone clause coordinated with the inherited-person-and-speech clause, so arrival is not a separate scene but the continuation of dispossession.

topics.headline: second conjunction joins possession and arrival
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the sentence pivot from divine taking to human arrival without breaking the verdict frame.
topics.reason: The conjunction coordinates the coming clause with the inheritance clause, and the attachment evidence marks that relation as strongly licensed.

words.gloss_range: coordinated coming-to-Us verb in which the claimant is the mover and God is the fixed endpoint of accountability
words.root_gloss_range: root range around coming, arriving, bringing, and giving; the local verb selects concrete arrival toward God, while gift/reception contrasts remain as reversal pressure
words.prose: {{ar:وَيَأْتِينَا}} ({{tr:wa-yaʾtīnā}}) moves the dispossessed claimant toward the divine endpoint. The attached destination suffix fixes where the motion ends, while the hidden third-person subject keeps the human grammatically small and without an independent title. The {{ar:أ ت ي}} ({{tr:ʾ-t-y}}) range includes giving and coming elsewhere, but here the local branch is arrival for account: the one who spoke of being given now comes to God, reversing signs coming to humans (20:126) and demands that a sign come to them (20:133). The verb also opens the slot for the final solitary state, and its same-surah coming-alone echo in 19:95 makes this individual arrival part of a larger eschatological pattern. The internal hamza catch adds a small audible arrest at the word that moves the boaster from speech into accountable presence.

topics.headline: the attached suffix fixes God as destination
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the claimant moves, but the destination is already fixed by the attached divine object-pronoun.
topics.reason: The local verb has a third-person masculine subject and a first-person plural clitic object complement, making God the encoded endpoint of the coming.

topics.headline: the human subject remains unnamed
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the boaster brought into motion without receiving an independent noun or title.
topics.reason: The subject is recoverable only through third-person morphology and prior context, while the written word visibly fuses coordination, motion, and destination.

topics.headline: root range narrows to arrival for account
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels the root's giving and coming range reverse the boast: the expected gift is replaced by the claimant's own arrival before God.
topics.reason: The local grammar selects coming to God, while the contrast with signs coming to humans (20:126), demands for a sign to come (20:133), and the boast of being given (19:77) supplies reversal pressure rather than a separate local gift sense.

topics.headline: arrival anticipates the coming-alone formula
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees this individual arrival as a preview of the same-surah universal coming-alone statement in 19:95.
topics.reason: The current coming-alone pairing is echoed by the universal formulation in 19:95, so the local individual case participates in a concrete same-surah pattern.

topics.headline: arrival verb opens the final state slot
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the verb does not close the ayah; it carries the claimant into the final condition named next.
topics.reason: The following accusative state depends on the coming verb, and the coming-alone pattern is made explicit again in 19:95.

topics.headline: internal catch suits the judgment motion
topics.reader_payoff: The reader can hear a small internal catch at the word that moves the boaster from speech into accountable presence.
topics.reason: The phonetic observation follows the visible word form and remains secondary to the grammar of motion and destination.

words.gloss_range: solitary arrival-state: alone, stripped of companion and claimed supports, as the final circumstantial condition of the one coming
words.root_gloss_range: root range around singleness, solitary separation, being without companion, and individualized standing; the local noun selects a concrete solitary state rather than bare numerical oneness
words.prose: {{ar:فَرْدًا}} ({{tr:fardan}}) is the final state in which the claimant arrives. Its accusative circumstantial role attaches aloneness to the coming subject, not to the divine endpoint, and its indefinite singular form leaves the solitude stark. The {{ar:ف ر د}} ({{tr:f-r-d}}) pressure is not mere arithmetic oneness; it is stripped, companionless arrival that answers the earlier wealth-and-children boast. The singular concrete noun isolates one claimant rather than using a plural-distributive group frame, so this man becomes the full instance of aloneness before the wider formula. Placed as the closing word, it turns the ayah's last audible fact into the human condition, while the recurrence in 19:95 lets this individual verdict preview universal solitary arrival. That field also contrasts the plea against being left alone (21:89) and the group-individual accountability formula (6:94), and the clipped final sound suits the reduction from boastful plurality to one bare arrival-state.

topics.headline: accusative state fixes aloneness at arrival
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees aloneness as the condition in which the claimant comes, not as a detached abstract idea.
topics.reason: The word is an accusative circumstantial state modifying the hidden subject of the coming verb, and the indefinite form leaves the state unqualified.

topics.headline: solitude reverses the wealth-and-children boast
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels the final word strip away the companions, lineage, and supports implied by the earlier boast.
topics.reason: The local context answers the claim of wealth and offspring in 19:77, and the root evidence supports solitary separation rather than neutral counting alone.

topics.headline: singular concrete noun individualizes the verdict
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the form isolates one claimant as the full instance of aloneness, rather than distributing a crowd into individuals.
topics.reason: The aligned word is singular and concrete, and the contrast with plural-distributive individual-coming formulas such as 6:94 clarifies but does not replace the local singular form.

topics.headline: rare solitary-arrival field links the verdict outward
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the individual solitary verdict tied to the same-surah universal formula in 19:95 and contrasted with the plea against being left alone in 21:89.
topics.reason: The recurrence with coming in 19:95, the plea against solitary abandonment in 21:89, and the plural-distributive accountability contrast in 6:94 give concrete intertextual pressure to the local final word.

topics.headline: final placement lands on stripped solitude
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the ayah close not on the divine act but on the claimant's reduced condition.
topics.reason: The circumstantial state is postposed to the end of the ayah, and the sound observation remains a secondary support for that clipped closure.

baseline_models.mechanism: The transfer verb removes the claimant and the content of his claim from his control; arrival then presents him without the attachments that made the claim substantial.

activation_trace.role: Transfer from a prior holder supplies the dispossession axis for claimant and claim.
Voiced speech supplies the residue explicitly governed by مَا.
Coming and reaching supply the terminal presentation before Us.
Unmixed singularity strips companions, possessions, and comparators from that presentation.

changed_reading.before: A person dies and leaves property behind.
changed_reading.after: The claimant and his voiced claim pass beyond his control, and he appears without the relations or goods on which the claim depended.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The inherited مَا يَقُولُ is juxtaposed with the speaker arriving فَرْدًا.
baseline_models.mechanism: Inheritance lets a claim outlast its holder; the القول branch as belief and the separated-pearl branch of فرد make the claim an inspectable remainder detached from its claimant.

activation_trace.role: Succession supplies survival of an item beyond its prior holder.
A القول as belief or position extends the object beyond its acoustic utterance.
Arrival supplies the moment at which holder and remainder are separately exposed.
A pearl separated in a string supplies the image of a discrete claim severed from its speaker.

changed_reading.before: What he says is a transient sound that remains attached to him.
changed_reading.after: His position becomes a separable remainder that survives for inspection while he arrives as a distinct, unsupported individual.

context_deltas.mechanism: The earlier first-person expectation of being given wealth and offspring reverses direction in the focus: what he anticipates receiving is inherited away, and the expected beneficiary arrives without it.

activation_trace.role: Inheritance supplies transfer away from the claimant rather than acquisition by him.
His actual coming to Us replaces his forecast of a gift coming to him.
Arrival alone supplies the result of the reversed acquisition.
The voiced assertion supplies the specific antecedent for what he says.
Giving supplies the expected direction of transfer toward the speaker.
Accumulated wealth supplies the material content of the expected gift.
Offspring supplies the relational content that singular arrival removes.

structural_cues: 19:77 and 19:80 repeat saying and coming with opposite persons and directions: he expects to be given, then he comes to Us.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies his stated gift, its wealth-and-offspring contents, inheritance, and lone arrival; I connect مَا يَقُولُ to that statement and read the agent reversal as dispossession. A live alternative is that only the assertion, not the named goods, is inherited.

changed_reading.before: The inheritance is a generic transfer after death.
changed_reading.after: It is a pointed reversal of his forecast: the would-be recipient loses title to the very wealth and lineage he expects, then arrives without either.

context_deltas.mechanism: The repeated phrase مَا يَقُولُ first enters writing that fixes judgment and then enters inheritance; speech therefore survives as a recorded liability whose consequence is extended.

activation_trace.role: Succession supplies custody of a residue after its speaker loses control.
The focus repeats the voiced object that the prior ayah writes.
Written fixation that entails judgment turns utterance into durable evidence.
The exact repeated speech object binds the written record to the inherited remainder.
Continuous lengthening supplies persistence from record into consequence.
Punitive pain identifies the liability attached to the preserved statement.

structural_cues: 19:79-80 repeat مَا يَقُولُ across the sequence write, extend, inherit.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies writing, the identical speech phrase, extended punishment, and inheritance; I infer a record-to-liability handoff. The live alternative is that writing and inheritance are parallel acts with no custodial arrow between them.

changed_reading.before: His words are only the content of a boast.
changed_reading.after: The boast becomes a durable evidentiary estate: fixed in writing, retained beyond him, and attached to an extending consequence.

context_deltas.mechanism: Objects deliberately acquired to reinforce their owners reverse into opposing counterparts; the focus singularity is therefore the endpoint of a failed support system, not merely physical solitude.

activation_trace.role: Unmixed singularity supplies the endpoint after coalition failure.
Deliberate acquisition supplies construction of the support network.
Reinforcement supplies the intended function of the acquired gods.
Submissive worship supplies the relation the supposed supporters repudiate.
Contrary opposition reverses support into an adverse counterparty.

structural_cues: 19:81 gives the purpose لِيَكُونُوا لَهُمْ عِزًّا; 19:82 negates it and replaces it with ضِدًّا.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies an acquired source of reinforcement and its explicit reversal into opposition; I connect that failed relation to فَرْدًا as the resulting social condition. A live alternative limits the focus solitude to wealth and offspring from 19:77.

changed_reading.before: He arrives alone simply because possessions cannot accompany him.
changed_reading.after: He arrives after a manufactured coalition collapses: intended reinforcers not only fail to accompany him but stand over against him.

context_deltas.mechanism: Intercession is the joining of another person to one standing alone, but the context denies ownership of that addition and makes covenant, not possession, its exception.

activation_trace.role: Being unjoined supplies the condition that an intercessor would alter.
Possession and disposal supply the leverage explicitly denied.
An intercessor joining another supplies the precise relational alternative to solitary standing.
A preserved covenant supplies the sole stated basis for that relation.

structural_cues: 19:87 uses a negation-exception construction: no owned intercession, except through a covenant with the Merciful.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies denied ownership, joining intercession, and a covenant exception; I infer that فَرْدًا excludes self-controlled advocacy. The live alternative is that 19:87 states a general rule without specifying this speaker's arrival.

changed_reading.after: Alone also means legally unaugmented: he cannot own a second voice to join his case, and any exception lies outside his claimed assets.

context_deltas.mechanism: The inheritance term opens a genealogical frame, but the later sequence denies that the Merciful acquires a child and recasts every claimant as an arriving servant; false filial attribution is reversed into ownership of claimant and claim.

activation_trace.role: Succession from predecessor to heir supplies the genealogical frame that the context overturns.
False attribution supplies a context-activated scope for what he says.
Saying what is not so identifies the later filial assertion as a false attribution.
Acquisition supplies the alleged divine act toward a child.
Biological offspring supplies the asserted lineage.
Claimed right or affiliation exposes the son statement as an attribution of relation.
Fitness and propriety supply the explicit denial that such acquisition can apply.
Servitude and ownership replace the fabricated filial relation.

structural_cues: 19:88-93 move from saying that the Merciful took a child, through repeated denial, to everyone coming as a servant.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies an inheritance image, repeated child attribution, its denial, and universal servitude; I use inheritance's lineage structure to connect them and read ownership as the reversal. The live alternative is that مَا يَقُولُ refers only to the wealth-and-child boast in 19:77, not the later divine-son claim.

changed_reading.before: The inherited saying concerns only a man's expected estate and descendants.
changed_reading.after: It can also answer speech that fabricates divine lineage: no child succeeds the Merciful; the speakers and their attribution instead return under ownership as servants.

context_deltas.mechanism: Plural cohorts can be gathered or driven toward the same authority, but exhaustive enumeration resolves the collective flow into one-by-one presentation; فَرْدًا names the unit of accounting, not absence of a universal gathering.

activation_trace.role: Coming to Us supplies the destination later shared by every cohort.
One-by-one arrival supplies the unit into which the cohorts are resolved.
Driving and gathering a group supplies collective movement toward one destination.
A delegation approaching authority supplies an honored collective arrival mode.
Driving and expulsion supply the coercive movement of the contrasting cohort.
Reaching a destination supplies the contrasting compelled arrival mode.
Exhaustive numerical survey supplies complete coverage of the gathered population.
Counting the counted supplies explicit unitization within that coverage.
Totality and enclosure prevent individualization from meaning only an exceptional person.
The repeated arrival root confirms the focus movement at universal scope.
The exact repeated singularity confirms one-by-one presentation as the final mode.

structural_cues: 19:85-86 present plural cohorts and contrasting arrival modes; 19:94-95 shift to exhaustive count and repeat ءَاتِيهِ ... فَرْدًا.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies collective routing, exhaustive counting, and the exact later repetition of coming alone; I infer a two-stage mechanism of group conveyance followed by individual accounting. The live alternative is that counting expresses knowledge without describing a processing sequence.

changed_reading.before: Coming alone excludes any collective scene.
changed_reading.after: Collective movement and individual presentation coexist: all are mustered in cohorts, but each claim and claimant is finally handled as a single counted case.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because it treats speech as materially load-bearing; it remains anchored in the focus قول and inheritance, while 19:88-90 explicitly moves from a false saying to near-fracture, splitting, and collapse. Render it as a context-driven causal image, not as a lexical meaning of يقول.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: مَا يَقُولُ is the inherited object.

activation_trace.role: Inheritance supplies persistence of the utterance after control passes from its speaker.
Voiced speech supplies the focus object that acquires structural consequence.
False attribution supplies the later saying from which the rupture sequence proceeds.
Opening and splitting supply the first material response to the saying.
Rending open supplies propagation of the utterance's load through the earth.
Severe breaking and demolition supply the terminal image of structural overload.

changed_reading.before: The saying is inert evidence that merely remains on record.
changed_reading.after: The inherited saying can be carried as an effective load whose false relation nearly tears the surrounding order apart.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is branch-distant because it activates the fire-stirring branch of ورث rather than ordinary succession; the exact focus root, its speech object, and 19:79's writing and extended punishment keep it anchored. Render only as an explicit branch metaphor, never as the direct translation of نرث.

activation_trace.role: Stirring embers until they ignite supplies an exploratory action image for what is done with the utterance.
Voiced speech supplies the material metaphorically treated as kindling.
Ordered letters and the written object supply preservation before ignition.
Continuous extension supplies duration to the ember-like consequence.
Punitive pain supplies the domain in which the stirred utterance burns.

changed_reading.before: Inheritance passively receives what survives the speaker.
changed_reading.after: Exploratorily, the preserved utterance is an ember actively stirred into an extending punitive consequence.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because it uses the packet's secondary ق و ل to ق ل ل mapping and links littleness, a separated pearl, and a hidden sound; it remains anchored in مَا يَقُولُ, inheritance, and فَرْدًا, with 19:98 ending in no detectable person or whisper. Render as a phonetic-branch activation, not as ordinary morphology.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: The saying is inherited while its speaker arrives فَرْدًا.

activation_trace.role: Succession supplies retention of a residue after the claimant is gone.
Littleness and diminution reduce the grand claim to a negligible remainder.
A separated pearl supplies the image of that remainder isolated from its owner.
Dispersal into individuals supplies the disappearance of the claimant's generation as a collective support.
Auditory detection supplies the test under which the remaining claim nearly vanishes.
A hidden low sound supplies the final minimal trace of once-expansive speech.

changed_reading.before: His boast projects abundant wealth, offspring, and social continuation.
changed_reading.after: The boast contracts into one negligible verbal bead: a barely detectable residue retained after claimant, cohort, and support have disappeared.

strongest_changes: 19:77 reverses the expected gift: wealth and offspring move from promised acquisition to inherited loss.
19:79 turns transient speech into a written liability that persists beyond its speaker.
19:81-87 makes lone arrival the collapse of acquired reinforcement and self-owned advocacy.
19:93-95 makes فردًا the unit of exhaustive accounting inside a universal gathering.
summary.what_was_special: The four focus roots form one transfer-and-presentation mechanism: speech asserts acquisition, inheritance reverses title, coming executes presentation, and singularity removes every claimed attachment. Later lineage, intercession, gathering, and exact lexical repetition sharpen distinct readings without forcing them into one interpretation.
remaining_uncertainties: The syntax can foreground either the claimant plus his saying or what is inherited from him; that scope affects how literally the named goods enter the transfer.
The later divine-son claim may directly expand مَا يَقُولُ or may only activate an analogous genealogical reversal.
The fire and ق ل ل readings are packet-licensed exploratory branches, not stable lexical renderings.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi, bir şeyin önceki sahibinden akrabalık ya da başka bir hak sebebiyle sonrakilere geçmesini; özellikle ölümden sonra malın mirasçıya kalmasını anlatır. Verilen dal çerçevesi bu aktarım yönünü ve miras ilişkisini doğru biçimde korur.

concept_map.definition: Bir malın ya da başka bir edinilmiş değerin önceki sahibinden, akrabalık veya geçerli başka bir sebep dolayısıyla mirasçıya geçmesidir. Miras sözü, önceki kuşaktan kalan kökeni veya kalıntıyı da gösterebilir.

facets.statement: Bir şey önce bir kişiye veya topluluğa aitken akrabalık ya da başka bir hak sebebiyle sonrakilere geçer.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi bir başkasını mirasçı veya malda pay sahibi kılmayı, bir şeyi ona miras bırakmayı ve ayrıca bir kimsenin bir şeye emek çekmeden kavuşmasını birlikte verir.
